papers.name: Where2comm
papers.b1_quote: The spatial conﬁdence generator generates a spatial conﬁdence map from the feature map
papers.b1: A confidence map from a detection decoder over the agent's own feature map.
papers.b2_quote: The request map of theith agent is R(k) i = 1− C(k) i
papers.b2: Split by round. The initial round is decided by the sending agent's own local confidence map alone; later rounds combine it with the receiver's request map from the previous round, which is Eq. (2). The ego's request therefore steers rounds after the first, not the first.
papers.sel: Which spatial regions to send, and to whom: a per-location binary mask over the BEV feature map, one mask per receiver.
papers.timing_note: initial round before the perception message; later rounds use the previous round's exchange
papers.b3_quote: the communication volume is log2 ( |M(k) i→j|× D× 32/8 )
papers.b3: Eq. (5) counts the selected feature volume: log2 of selected cells x channels x 4 bytes. The request map is H x W and does not appear in that formula.
papers.implication: Its decision input is the ego's own detection confidence, kept as a spatial map over locations.

papers.name: When2com
papers.b1_quote: compresses its local observationsxi into a com- pact query vectorµi and a key vectorκi
papers.b1: A learned low-dimensional query from the agent's own raw observation.
papers.b2_quote: We further broad- cast the query to all of other agents
papers.b2: Both sides: the ego broadcasts a query, every other agent holds a key, and the match sets the connection weights.
papers.sel: Whom to connect to and how strongly: the communication group and its connection weights, pruned by an activation.
papers.timing_note: the query and key are formed from local observations before the handshake runs
papers.b3_label_note: a table header, not a section heading: this paper's experiment-section headings did not survive PDF extraction, so no section number is claimed
papers.b3: MBytes per frame and links per agent, against 2.5 / 5 for the fully connected baselines. The text also states a one-fourth bandwidth ratio, but that sentence is interrupted by a figure's axis labels in the extraction and is therefore not quoted. The query's own size is not itemised.
papers.implication: The decision needs a key from every candidate, so it is not formed by the ego alone.

papers.name: Who2com
papers.b1_quote: compute a matching score, s ji, between their keys, κi∈ Rk, and the request message
papers.b1: A learned key from each candidate's own observation, scored against the requester's compressed request.
papers.b2_quote: the de- graded agent ﬁrst broadcasts its request message
papers.b2: Both sides, in three stages: request from the ego, scores back from candidates, then the ego connects.
papers.sel: Whom to receive from: the best n agents, each then sending one full feature map.
papers.timing_note: the three-stage handshake completes before the selected agent sends its feature map
papers.b3_quote: comparable to centralized ones using a quarter of the bandwidth
papers.b3: A ratio in the abstract; the selection sends one feature map where centralized baselines send all. The request and the returned scores are not itemised.
papers.implication: The score that decides is computed by the candidates, not by the ego.

papers.name: Select2Col
papers.b1_quote: each node corresponds to an agent and comprises its sparse map along with the semantic
papers.b1: A GNN over per-agent nodes, each holding that agent's sparse feature map and its information latency.
papers.b2_quote: receives semantic information transmitted by its neighboring agents
papers.b2: Collaborator-side, and only after arrival: the sparse maps forming the GNN nodes are the received semantic information.
papers.sel: Which collaborators to keep and how to weight them for fusion; agents below a weight threshold are dropped.
papers.b3: Not itemised for the decision itself; the paper models transmission latency instead. No estimate is offered, because the quantity would be the cost of something this process does not do.
papers.implication: A process of a different shape: it decides after receiving, so its decision information is not of a kind the ego holds beforehand.

papers.name: SmartCooper
papers.b1_quote: dynamically adjust the compression ratio based on the channel state information
papers.b1: Channel state information sets the compression ratio; sensing-coverage overlap drives the judger.
papers.b2_quote: our judger scores reconstructed image sequences based on the union of sensing coverage
papers.b2: Split: CSI is available before transmission, but the judger scores data already transmitted and reconstructed at the ego.
papers.sel: The compression ratio per vehicle, and whether reconstructed data is admitted to fusion at all.
papers.timing_note: the CSI half is before the message; the judger half is after reconstruction, and the row is classified by the judger
papers.b3_quote: a substantial reduction in communication costs by 23.10%
papers.b3: A ratio against a no-judger scheme. Since the judger runs after reconstruction, the saving falls on later rounds rather than on the transmission being judged. Not itemised for the decision.
papers.implication: A process of a different shape: its channel half is pre-transmission, its task half needs the data first.

papers.name: CoDS
papers.venue: “CoDS: Collaborative Perception via Digital Semantic Communication”, Jipeng Gan, Le Liang, Hua Zhang, Chongtao Guo, Shi Jin, arXiv 2512.22513
papers.b1_quote: the spatial compression ratio as the fraction of featu res selected for transmission
papers.b1: A selection mask over the sender's own BEV feature map, plus SNR for modulation and code rate.
papers.b2_quote: the CA V ﬁrst employs a feature extraction network
papers.b2: Sender-side, before transmission: the CAV decides what of its own features to send. The ego does not request.
papers.sel: Which of its own feature cells to send, the channel compression ratio, and the modulation order and code rate.
papers.b3_quote: Channel Uses = Qd × q C × γs × Rc × log2 Or
papers.b3: Also expressed in Channel Uses. Whether it is the same accounting as ours is not settled here: code rate, modulation order, the mask or index overhead, packet headers, and whether a failed message is still charged all remain to be checked against our chain.
papers.implication: The nearest transmission accounting to ours, with the decision sitting at the sender about its own data.

papers.name: SemHARQ
papers.b1_quote: the gradients of the task performance with respect to the features are considered
papers.b1: Feature importance from task-performance gradients at the transmitter; distortion of received features at the receiver.
papers.b2_quote: generate a binary feedback vector p(j+1)
papers.b2: Both, but only after a first transmission: the receiver evaluates what arrived and feeds back which features to resend.
papers.sel: Which features to send first, how many per round, and which corrupted features to retransmit.
papers.timing_note: the importance ranking is formed at the transmitter before sending, but the retransmission decision requires the first transmission to have happened
papers.b3: No figure for the feedback overhead is given. Estimated: one bit per feature of the block just received, so B bits per retransmission round.
papers.b3_assumption: Assumes the binary vector p is uncoded, one bit per feature of the block just received, and sent once per round; the paper states the vector and its indexing but gives neither a length in bits nor a channel for it.
papers.implication: A process of a different shape: its ranking is retrospective, needing a transmission before it can rank.
